claim: 'A plan defect is reported, not repaired' does not say what tree state a partially-applied failed attempt leaves behind, so a retry after strike one may start from a dirty tree the plan never assumed.

Two-strikes escalation needs a durable per-item counter surviving separate fresh spawns, but no storage location is named anywhere in the design, so a compaction or fresh orchestrator invocation silently resets it.

The validator re-runs the verify block with no stated isolation from the executor's mutated worktree, so a non-idempotent assertion can produce a FAIL the frozen-criteria contract cannot distinguish from a regression.

Nothing in the executor contract names a file-reservation step, despite sibling sessions and autosync being live risks, so concurrently-dispatched executors have no stated way to avoid stomping each other.

The gate is defined on output-token share, but the doc's own diagnosis puts 85% of main-thread cost in context, not generation; a goal can pass the gate with 300K-context orchestrator turns intact, or fail it while cutting cost 60%. CONFIRMED live: 86% output share (gate failed) alongside 35% cost share against an 85% baseline (objective met).

Pilot-1's 6/6 gauge defects mean the validator's sole yardstick is frequently broken, yet the validator has no channel to distinguish 'criteria wrong' from 'execution wrong' — both produce an identical FAIL-with-quoted-criterion. The problem statement and the gate rest entirely on profile.py's lane-attribution rules, and no validation of that instrument is cited — an unvalidated meter one level below the gate formula.

claim: Adjudication of f-004 vs f-020: not one contradiction but two regimes of one gap. f-020's citation over-reaches (the 0/6 belongs to the reading-based review step, not to re-execution). Three configurations separate: reading (0/6), gauge-lint's pre-freeze decoupled dry-run (6/6), and Pattern F's post-hoc replay against mutated state (never measured).

Pattern F cites pilot-1's 6/6 by name to justify escalation but never adopts rule 9 — the mandatory pre-freeze gauge dry-run, blocking, by a model other than the plan's author, wired as step 0 of /plan-review — the mechanism doctrine built in direct response to that same finding.

CONFIRMED: no plan field, executor or validator contract, or orchestrator script anywhere checks commit SHA, branch, or clean tree; executing-plans' one SHA artifact (vetted_sha) is written after verification, a postcondition. grep over orchestrate.py returns zero state checks.

The run:/expect: mechanism could carry a baseline-SHA assertion today with no new tooling, but the template's worked example, Must-Haves categories and Remember checklist never prompt for one — so the precondition gap replicates into every plan by construction, not by author oversight.

Q-E names plan drift as Pattern F's likely novel failure mode, yet none of the four 'what makes it enforceable' bullets addresses it — the doc's enforceability claim is falsified by its own open-questions section.

The gate's denominator scales with item count and the per-item re-priming cost never enters it at all. Arbitrage direction INVERTED by live data (main 70K output vs 13K from all subagents: executors copy plans, so fragmenting raises the numerator faster). Cost term CONFIRMED and understated: subagent lanes moved 30.9M cache-read tokens against the main thread's 9.8M.

Fresh context is mandated once per executor and once per validator with no stated reason and no batching alternative examined, leaving the largest fixed-cost lever spent by default rather than by decision. CONFIRMED live: 253 Sonnet + 93 Opus messages across 5 items.

Pilot-1's 6/6 gauge-defect rate is shakedown data the cited source frames as process-immaturity evidence, not a steady-state rate. Now self-referential: the journal draws a steady-state Q-A conclusion from five first-run pilots.

CONFIRMED: the 'repo path' handoff names no worktree isolation or interlock reservation, and this exact gap already produced two live failures in this goal's own pilot run — a stale-branch checkout and a concurrent old-parser writer collision — both caught by luck.

Both live collisions were triaged as ordinary per-plan gauge defects, fixed by correcting one verify assertion, rather than as a contract-level isolation gap — so the fix does not close the class and the enforceability section is unchanged by the run that surfaced both.

claim: CONFIRMED: profile.py's lane decision never reads `model`, so a model:inherit frontier subagent buckets identically to a cheap Sonnet executor; the gate can PASS on a goal where every turn, main and subagent, ran the frontier model. The per-(lane,model) rows already computed contain the data; the gate scalar never reads that column.

profile.py has no bead or goal argument at all — only --session/--days/--since/--until — while the gate's unit is 'the goal'. --session undercounts a multi-session goal, --days co-mingles unrelated ones. CONFIRMED live: the journal's own number was taken with --session.

The main/subagent split is three undocumented path/flag proxies OR'd together with no semantic tie to 'this is a Pattern F role turn' and no version pin to the transcript-layout convention. CONFIRMED live: the journal's table carries a Haiku 4.5 row, 30 messages, counted as offloaded execution.

The durable verdict register that would make this pattern self-correcting already exists (_interspect_insert_evidence in execute-plan.md), but Pattern F never states whether it routes through that call site; the write is fail-open at three layers, and its schema (bare `pass` boolean, escalation_count hardcoded 0) cannot distinguish independent confirmation from mechanical replay. CONFIRMED live: five pilot verdicts recorded only in a hand-typed markdown table.

'Frozen criteria' freezes text, not repo state; three spawns touch an unpinned trunk with no pin or lease at any of them; Q-E scopes drift to the executor and misses the validator-side case; and the only coordination fix — pin the commit — collapses the validator's re-run into guaranteed-identical replay.

CONFIRMED (self-labeled near-exact restatement of f-038): profile.py's lane classification never consults the model field, so main_output_share collapses the model dimension within a lane and can pass on a goal whose non-main tokens were all frontier-generated.

The smallest viable fix for the inherit-laundering gap already exists and is already imported: cost.py's get_pricing classifies any model string into a tier by substring match, profile.py imports it, and the sole call site feeds only calc_cost — never the lane bucket the gate reads.

The exhaustive two-remedy escalation contract has no branch for a codex-lane strike caused by sandbox capability rather than plan defect, and Q-C's framing presupposes a 'parity' check defined nowhere in the doc.

The 'Inheritance closed' bullet, filed under 'what makes it enforceable rather than aspirational', enforces only which model answers at 48 command sites and 25 agents — it installs none of Pattern F's actual message contract (frozen criteria, verbatim reporting, no scope expansion) at any of them.

The raw transcript substrate that produced this document's own unrequested headline finding survives under Pattern F, but the tool answers only three pre-defined questions and the design names no owner or cadence for the open-ended read across dispersed subagent transcripts.
